title: Nuclear moonlighting of arsenic metabolic enzymes and reprogramming-resistant epimutations
text:
The epigenome is remarkably responsive to environmental cues and is a central player in the
transcriptional and physiological response to environmental exposures. However, how environmental
chemicals trigger a deregulation of the epigenome that is maintained over the course of development is still
poorly understood. Our research program will seek to transform our understanding of the mechanism of action
of environmental chemicals by examining the role of metabolic enzymes in directing reprogramming-resistant
epimutations.

title: Targeting PEN-GPR83 as a as a strategy to reduce opioid abuse liability
text:
The mainline treatments for pain are opioid analgesics which are unfortunately accompanied by significant side
effects including tolerance, dependence, and addiction. A novel receptor system PEN-GPR83 regulates
morphine antinociception however, the neurobiological mechanism by which this interaction occurs is
unknown. The long-term goal of this project is to reveal mechanism by which PEN-GPR83 decouples the
beneficial from the detrimental effects of opioids.

title: Sensory neuron-mast cell crosstalk in IBS pathophysiology
text:
Abdominal pain is the primary driver of healthcare utilization by patients with irritable bowel
syndrome (IBS), however, available treatments for abdominal pain in IBS are limited,
untargeted, symptom-based, and often ineffective. This is partly due to a lack of a better
understanding of underlying pathogenic mechanisms. The overall goal of this project is to
delineate the mechanisms of how sensory neuron-mediated activation of MRGPRX2 receptor
on a subset of colonic mast cells contributes to visceral hypersensitivity and barrier dysfunction
in IBS, thereby identifying a novel pathway for therapeutic target and an IBS subpopulation who
will benefit from this targeted treatment.

title: Inhibitory corticostriatal circuit mechanisms underlying binge alcohol drinking
text:
While cortical glutamatergic inputs to the dorsolateral striatum have been extensively studied in the context of
habitual and compulsive alcohol-seeking, little is known about the role of cortical GABAergic inhibitory inputs to
the dorsolateral striatum. This project seeks to identify a novel mechanism of alcohol action on inhibitory
parvalbumin-expressing neurons in the anterior insular cortex that project directly to the dorsolateral striatum.
By integrating electrophysiology, in vivo and ex vivo optogenetics, chemogenetics, and binge alcohol drinking
paradigms, we will determine how alcohol alters corticostriatal inhibitory synapses and how these synapses
contribute to excessive alcohol consumption and aversive drinking behavior, with the long-term goal of this
research is to identify circuit-based therapeutic targets that could restore inhibitory balance in alcohol use
disorder and inform new treatment strategies for alcohol addiction.

title: Translating Medical Device Discoveries to the Bedside: The Academic Entrepreneurship Awareness to Action (AE2A) Curriculum to Promote Training of a Diverse Workforce
text:
This IPERT will help educate the biomedical research workforce of the future in the skills necessary to engage
in the broad ecosystem for medical device development across the lifespan. The programming includes case-
based coursework, experiential learning, and networking and mentoring opportunities to help participants
develop and deepen their skills in reviewing and evaluating medical device proposals. Creation of Individual
Development Plans and mentoring teams to support growth for two years following a bootcamp will deepen
participants’ expertise, and sustained engagement in medical device development will be tracked during and
after the programming to measure impact.

title: Positioning Mason's Regional Biocontainment Laboratory for Effective Pandemic Preparedness
text:
OVERALL COMPONENT
George Mason University’s Regional Biocontainment Lab serves as a center for scientific
collaboration to 1) generate advanced knowledge of pathogen biology and host interaction
mechanisms, and 2) evaluate diagnostics, therapeutics and vaccines. This proposal addresses
existing gaps and opportunities with solutions to enhance a) safety practices, b) facilities and
operations management, and c) research capabilities to more effectively face sudden disease
outbreaks and support a more robust pipeline of innovations for response to future pandemics,
while continuing to comply with NIAID, CDC, and UDSA/APHIS regulations.

title: Correlative Optical Tweezers-Fluorescence Microscope from LUMICKS for Basic and Translational Research at Georgetown University
text:
Georgetown University investigators at the College of Arts and Sciences and the Georgetown University Medical
Center perform basic biomedical and translational studies, aimed at obtaining fundamental knowledge to
advance human health. Users in this proposal have a wide variety of projects, including protein kinase regulation,
development of RNA-based biosensors, RNA interactions with small molecules, homeostatic control of synaptic
transmission, potassium channel regulation, role of droplet formation in nuclear pore protein function, drug
resistance in malaria, among others. The acquisition of the LUMICKS C-Trap Dymo, the first and only commercial
instrument combining optical tweezers, high-resolution fluorescence imaging and sophisticated microfluidics, will
significantly advance these studies by allowing Georgetown University investigators to address unknown
mechanisms underlying the function of biomolecules involved in normal and in disease states.

title: NextGen Oncology Scholars: Nurturing Tomorrow's Pioneers
text: In response to the critical need for skilled researchers in the rapidly evolving field of cancer biology, our proposal introduces the NextGen Oncology Scholars: Nurturing Tomorrow’s Pioneers program, aimed at cultivating a new generation of researchers with hands-on experience and life skills essential for breakthrough innovations in cancer treatment and prevention. This R25 research experience program at the Wayne State University and the Barbara Ann Karmanos Comprehensive Cancer Center leverages our established research and training infrastructure to provide exceptional undergraduate scholars with dynamic, hands-on training in cancer biology research, preparing them for advanced graduate studies and impactful careers in the field. Building on the success of our Cancer Biology Summer Undergraduate Fellowship Program, our proposed program offers a holistic training approach that combines laboratory research, in-class learning, and clinical exposure. The goal is to foster growth of emerging researchers equipped with the knowledge and communication skills, needed to drive innovations and advancements in cancer biology research and treatment in the coming decades.

title: Small-molecule exploitation of ZBP1-driven nuclear necroptosis for cancer immunotherapy
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE.
Many patients do not respond to immunotherapies, including immune checkpoint blockade (ICB), because their
tumors are not sufficiently immunogenic, and thus go undetected by their immune systems. In this proposal,
we outline a new small-molecule approach to increasing the immunogenicity of tumors by harnessing a
recently-discovered inflammatory cell death modality, which we term nuclear necroptosis. The successful
completion of the proposed research will outline an entirely new strategy to activate a highly inflammatory form
of necroptosis and potentiate ICB-based immunotherapies, with important clinical ramifications.

title: Defining the Role of Viral Infections and Autoantibodies in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Progression
text:
This application uses data from a large group of well-characterized subjects from the COPDGene Study, which
includes 5 and 10 year follow-ups and extensive available genomics datasets. We will use the state-of-the-art
Phage ImmunoPrecipitation Sequencing (PhIP-seq) technology to efficiently and comprehensively profile 3,000
blood samples for autoantibodies and antibodies from prior viral infections. We will determine whether infections
with certain viruses and/or the development of specific autoantibodies are associated with more rapid
progression of COPD.

title: TR&D Project 2
text: TR&D2 Abstract The goal of TR&D #2 is to bioengineer nanoimmunomaterial tools (NIMs) through the design and synthesis of new biomaterials and nanoparticles (NPs) created for immunomodulation. This TR&D is driven by the needs of CPs and SPs for safe, effective, and targeted tools to genetically manipulate immune cells ex vivo and in vivo. Specifically, we will engineer NIMs’ chemical structure, physical properties, and surface coating with biologics to maximize cell-specific intracellular delivery of nucleic acids to program immune cells. TR&D #2 focuses on genetically engineering three specific types of immune cells (dendritic cells, macrophages, and T cells), including applications to stimulate or suppress reactivity to antigens in vivo in a targeted, cell-specific fashion. NIMs will be evaluated for applications to human health, including oncology and autoimmunity. NIMs will be made available to be utilized as an enabling technology by the other TR&Ds as the NIMs are synthesized, characterized, and validated. Additionally, the NIMs will be made available to CP collaborators, SP projects, and the broader bioengineering and immunology communities as tools for investigators to further their own research goals. TR&D2 supports and aligns with the Johns Hopkins Translational ImmunoEngineering (JH-TIE) vision in its use of engineering principles (Chemical Engineering, Materials Science & Engineering, and Biomedical Engineering) to design enabling immunoengineering technology and advance immunotherapy.

title: Dynamic Imaging of Lung Ventilation and Perfusion Using CT and MRI
text:
Advances in Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) now support regional imaging of lung structures
with CT-like contrast and high spatial resolution. The versatility of MRI data acquisition includes
motion detection that can be used to track changes in lung inflation and oxygen distribution during
free-breathing. This project will develop oxygen-enhanced imaging of ventilation of the lungs and
high-resolution acquisition of lung anatomy in a single, free-breathing 7-minute acquisition using
3D ultra-short time to echo MRI and study multiple chronic lung diseases to establish utility and
reproducibility.

title: Population and evolutionary dynamics of recombining genes and alleles in bacteria
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because understanding the causes,
mechanisms, constraints and consequences of genetic recombination is critical to pathogen evolution.
Thus, this proposal is relevant to the part of NIGMS’s mission that pertains to fostering fundamental
creative discoveries and innovative research strategies related to genetic mechanisms and evolutionary
processes to help reduce the burden of bacterial diseases and ultimately protect human health.

title: Leveraging high-throughput functional data for assessment of Alzheimer's risk
text:
Early risk stratification and intervention in Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias are vital as new
treatments emerge. The MAVEvidence platform developed by Constantiam Biosciences overcomes a critical
bottleneck in genetic testing by enabling clinical classification of difficult-to-interpret DNA variants associated
with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias, thereby facilitating earlier and more accurate risk
assessment. This breakthrough will enable earlier risk assessment, more appropriate care, and access to
clinical trials.

title: Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy Platform Study Reveals Mechanisms of Response in Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC)
text:
Most patients who undergo surgery to remove liver cancers experience recurrence of their cancer within a few
years. We are conducting a clinical trial of immunotherapy before potentially curative surgery for liver cancer,
and are investigating the effect of a brief course of immunotherapy on the removed cancers, to understand if
immunotherapy can change the cancers to improve cure rates.

title: Varenicline as a Treatment for Cannabis Use Disorder
text:
Cannabis use is prevalent and increasing, yet an efficacious pharmacotherapy for cannabis use disorder (CUD)
has yet to be identified. Varenicline has shown significant promise for CUD; however, further work is necessary
to fully evaluate its potential utility in women and to identify individuals who will benefit most from varenicline
treatment. This study will evaluate the efficacy of varenicline for CUD in a randomized controlled trial
incorporating cognitive behavioral therapy as a psychosocial treatment platform with equal numbers of men and
women and will apply machine-learning techniques to identify treatment responders.

title: Combating Chronic Liver Diseases via Understanding and Engineering Cell Competition and Fitness
text:
Health Relevance/Narrative:
Liver cells from fetal liver can provide a unique regenerative cell source to generate new healthy tissue
mass. We have identified the underlying mechanism and developed methods to produce similar growth-
advantaged cells in vitro. Our studies will dissect the mechanism of cell competition/fitness and how it
impacts chronic liver disease progression. Results from our proposed studies will provide new information
for developing novel cell-based therapies in patients with liver disease.

title: Contextual factors influencing cannabis use and behavioral economic demand in the natural environment
text:
Heavy cannabis use is associated with increased rates of negative consequences, including motor vehicle
crash fatalities, cannabis-associated emergency department visits, cannabis-induced psychosis, and cannabis
use disorder. Understanding the context surrounding cannabis use is important, considering that certain social
situations, physical locations, and upcoming activities have been shown to differentially predict cannabis use
and how much people value cannabis in laboratory studies. The proposed study will be the first to use mobile
technology to examine how the reinforcing value of cannabis and its consumption are impacted by daily
activities, social situations, and substance use contexts in the natural environment.

title: Evaluation of Guideline-based Uptake of Indicated Diagnostic exams after AbNormal Cervical cancer screening test in safEty-net settings (E-GUIDANCE)
text:
Despite high cervical cancer screening rates among uninsured populations, these groups are much more likely
to be diagnosed and die from cervical cancer, especially in safety-net health settings. This is possibly due to
multilevel barriers (including the fragmentation of care that separates primary care clinics from diagnostic care
housed in safety-net tertiary health centers) that delay follow-up care after an abnormal cervical cancer screening
test result. Following the ORBIT Model, a structured, systematic, and progressive approach to developing robust,
effective interventions, the proposed research aims to develop an intervention to address the multilevel barriers
to timely follow-up care after an abnormal cervical cancer screening test result across various safety-net health
settings.

title: The Molecular and Cellular Basis of Infectious Diseases (MCBID) Program
text:
This application requests funding for 8 PhD students to train in our Molecular and Cellular Basis of Infectious
Diseases (MCBID) training program. Our goal is to train future investigators in areas that are highly relevant to
national interests in topics related to infectious diseases and public health. The program trains young scientists
in the molecular aspects of pathogen biology and disease pathogenesis, as well as the ecology of disease,
epidemiology, and the role of vectors in pathogen transmission.
